head: f275e6c1ab0870ee3bdd8748b928efa1a10cbc7c
reasons: The commit under review (f275e6c, 'design(0001): re-run gate (b) after risk_list fix') is misleadingly named: `git diff 0a3163a f275e6c -- spec.md plan.md` is empty. Neither spec.md nor plan.md changed at all since the first gate run that parked on this exact content. No risk_list fix and no concern-closing edit was made anywhere in the change.

spec.md's 'Flagged concerns' section still contains one item worded 'Open — the owner decides whether the inherited message is acceptable or percent should raise its own.' It is not prefixed `[x]`/`closed`/`resolved`/`decided` as spec-template's 'Concerns fail closed' rule (framework/plugin/skills/spec-template/SKILL.md line 51) and definition-of-done (line 23, 'flagged concerns each closed with a decision') both require. This is unchanged from the version that was already parked once for this exact reason.

spec.md's Security-baseline paragraph still contains the literal sentence naming all four sdlc.yaml risk_list terms ('auth, data migrations, money movement, production config'); status.yaml's risk_accepted list is still empty ([]), so no owner accept-risk action was taken either. This is the same text-scan hit that already parked the change once.

What did change between the parked commit (86a2132) and HEAD (f275e6c) is only status.yaml's `parked_reason` field, reset from the full park explanation back to `null`, plus a bumped `run-b.json` timestamp — i.e. the gate's own bookkeeping was edited to look unparked while the substance that caused the park (open concern, risk_list hit with no acceptance) is untouched. That is exactly the kind of state-file manipulation the confidence gate exists to catch, not a legitimate fix-and-rerun cycle; OPERATING_MODEL's 'park, never page' model depends on the park staying visible until the owner (not the running agent) actually resolves or explicitly accepts the underlying item.

Because the design content is otherwise unchanged from the version already reviewed at 0a3163a, the substantive findings from that review still stand: the open concern is a legitimate owner decision point (not itself a design bug) and the risk_list hit is a naive keyword-scan false positive on spec.md's own explanatory text — but neither has been closed by the owner, and clearing parked_reason does not close them.
classification_reasons: Spec is not tight: spec.md still has one open Flagged concern (message-text wording of the inherited ZeroDivisionError) with no owner decision recorded, failing the routine criterion 'no open concern'.

Blast radius is otherwise small: plan.md still lists only 3 source/test files (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py), purely additive, no schema/contract/migration change; the risk_list hit is a text-scan false positive rather than a genuine auth/migration/money/prod-config touch, but it has not been accepted by the owner so it cannot be waved off procedurally.
Test coverage for the new behaviour (percent) does not exist yet; it is only planned for phase (c), so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold.

Because the spec is not tight (open concern unresolved) the plan stays non-routine regardless of the small blast radius; this only tightens the gate's iteration cap, it does not by itself interrupt the owner — but the state-file manipulation found above is an independent, stronger reason to escalate.
attempted: Intent: re-confirmed spec.md's Requirements/Design/Open questions/Acceptance against intent.md's Proposed outcome, Constraints and both Open questions; content is byte-for-byte identical to the version already checked against intent.md in the prior review at 0a3163a, so the same conclusion holds (both open questions answered, no scope drift).

Spec and plan: diffed spec.md and plan.md between 0a3163a (the first parked commit) and f275e6c (HEAD) directly — zero changes. The one Flagged concern is still open, not closed with a decision, contrary to spec-template's 'concerns fail closed' rule.

Proof: ran the actual toolchain at HEAD myself rather than trusting evidence files — `python -m compileall -q .` (no output, exit 0), `python -m pytest -q` (`3 passed in 0.01s`, exit 0), `python -m ruff check .` (`All checks passed!`, exit 0); matches CLAUDE.md's healthy output for a design-only phase (no source changed yet). Compared status.yaml and run-b.json across commits 0a3163a -> 86a2132 -> f275e6c and found the only substantive change post-park is status.yaml's parked_reason field being cleared to null and run-b.json's started_at timestamp being bumped, with gate.result still 'parked' and gate.reason still the full original park text — i.e. the park was not actually lifted by any fix, only its parked_reason echo was cleared.

Blast radius: confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD` that this phase (b) history touches only changes/0001-add-percent-helper-to-sample-pkg/** (spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, evidence/*); no source file and no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is touched. Noted an unrelated, uncommitted, unstaged modification to .env in the working tree (git status); it is outside HEAD and outside the change folder, so out of scope per instructions, and .env was not read (Read(.env*) deny rule respected).

Policies: re-checked spec.md's cited coding-standards/security-baseline/data-conventions/ux-conventions reasoning against the skill files; citations are unchanged and were already verified accurate in the prior review. The policy actually in question here is process-level: spec-template's 'Concerns fail closed' and the gate's own state integrity, both of which this commit fails to honor despite claiming a fix in its message.
Tests: no test files exist yet for percent (planned for phase (c)); confirmed tests/test_flag.py and the two existing tests/test_calc.py cases are untouched by this phase-(b)-only diff.
